verdict: Yes for a B2B-first founder, no if you plan to win retail freezers on day one. Frozen momos were the very first pitch on Shark Tank India, and BluePine Foods won ₹75 lakh because it had already built B2B supply to hotels and restaurants. That is still the route that works: steady orders from cafés and caterers first, retail and quick commerce once you can supply reliably.
angle: Momos are among the most-ordered snacks in north and east India, and cafés, hostels and caterers buy frozen momos to avoid hiring skilled hands for folding. Quick-commerce apps have also made frozen snacks an impulse buy in metros. The product is simple to make, which is exactly why competition is heavy: your edge has to come from consistency, a filling that stands out, and cold-chain reliability.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start a frozen momos business?
faq.a: A small unit supplying cafés and caterers in one city can start at ₹3–6 lakh for equipment, deep freezers, packaging and licences. A licensed unit with a blast freezer and cold room costs ₹40 lakh or more.

faq.q: Do I need an FSSAI licence for frozen momos?
faq.a: Yes. Any food business needs FSSAI registration, and a manufacturing unit above ₹12 lakh turnover needs a state licence. Retail packs also need Legal Metrology labelling.

faq.q: Who buys frozen momos in bulk?
faq.a: Cafés, college canteens, hostels, caterers, cloud kitchens and small restaurants are the steadiest buyers. They order weekly and value consistent quality over brand names.

faq.q: What did Shark Tank India say about frozen momos?
faq.a: BluePine Foods pitched frozen momos in Season 1, Episode 1, asking ₹50 lakh for 5% and closing at ₹75 lakh for 16% from three sharks. Their strength was an existing B2B and HoReCa business with a clear revenue track record.
